who: James W. Cook, historian of U.S. culture at Michigan since 2001; PhD U.S. history, Berkeley, 1996.

evidence.says: CV lists Michigan history appointments from 2001 and a 1996 Berkeley PhD in U.S. history; publications include The Arts of Deception.
Authority identifies James W. Cook, author of The Arts of Deception, and cites his 1996 dissertation as James Wallace Cook, Jr., a Berkeley PhD candidate.
Alternative authority identifies Captain James Cook, explorer and navigator, author of eighteenth-century voyage accounts.

notes: Doctorate and Michigan appointment agree. The explorer candidate p-127567 is a different person.

who: James Richard Farr, historian of early modern France at Purdue; PhD Northwestern, 1983.

Authority identifies James Richard Farr, author of Hands of Honor; its Work, Status, and Culture citation describes a Purdue history professor specializing in French history.
Alternative authority identifies James Barker Farr, author of Black Argonauts.

notes: Purdue affiliation, field, and doctorate match. Alternative p-40374 is James Barker Farr, a distinct author.

who: James L. Giblin, historian of Tanzania and East Africa at Iowa, 1986–2025; PhD Wisconsin–Madison, 1986.

Authority identifies James Leonard Giblin, author of The Politics of Environmental Control in Northeastern Tanzania; a citation describes James Giblin as an Iowa professor of African history.

notes: Authority, university, field, and exact doctorate institution/year agree.

who: Thomas William Heyck, historian of Britain and Ireland at Northwestern; PhD Texas at Austin.

Authority identifies Thomas William Heyck, also published as T. W. Heyck, and describes him as Northwestern professor emeritus of British and Irish history.

who: Alan I Marcus, historian of science, technology, and agriculture at Iowa State and Mississippi State; PhD history, Cincinnati, 1979.

evidence.says: Faculty page lists a Cincinnati history PhD in 1979, Iowa State appointments in 1980–2005, and Mississippi State appointments from 2005.
Authority identifies Alan I Marcus, author of Agricultural Science and the Quest for Legitimacy and Plague of Strangers, both listed on his Mississippi State page.
Alternative authority identifies Alan Rudolph Marcus, author of Out in the Cold and Relocating Eden.
UConn professor Alan Marcus works in curriculum and instruction and has a Stanford PhD in Curriculum and Teacher Education.
Alan S. Marcus authority cites Celluloid Blackboard, rather than the science and agriculture works of Alan I Marcus.

notes: Both advising institutions and the exact doctorate match p-136123. Alan R. Marcus and the two Alan S. Marcus candidate records are different from this supervisor.

who: Richard McGee Morse, Latin American historian at Yale, 1962–1972; PhD Columbia, 1952.

evidence.says: Yale finding aid identifies Richard McGee Morse, his Columbia PhD in 1952, Yale history appointments from 1962, Latin American Studies chairmanship, and departure in 1972.
Authority identifies Richard M. (Richard McGee) Morse, a Latin America historian who taught at Yale and Stanford; works include Cultura urbana latinoamericana.

notes: Exact doctorate institution/year, Yale affiliation, and field support identity. Yale records his departure in 1972; the later AHA student completion years do not establish continued Yale employment.

who: William J. Novak, historian of American law and regulation, formerly Chicago history, now Michigan law; PhD Brandeis, 1991.

Authority identifies William J. Novak and cites Michigan Law describing his legal history research and previous Chicago history professorship.

notes: Authority and exact doctorate match. His move in 2009 precedes the latest listed Chicago completion in 2011; it does not contradict the identity match.
